title: Joint normalization natural on bounded-flat tower maps
statement: Use flat telescopes and stage-induced maps as defined in [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map]. Let f:Z->Y be a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], with the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], derived pullback F [def-pc-derived-pullback], additive termwise tensor pullback H [def-pc-module-pullback], recorded tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], and canonical tensor shifts [def-sc-scheme-canonical-tensor-shift] and shifted-unit comparison c [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso]. Fix a supplied strong monoidal structure on F. A flat telescope is literally P=Cone(id_B-shift_t), where B=the countable coproduct of a sequence E_n of bounded-above complexes with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and t_n:E_n->E_(n+1); shift_t is specified on summand n by t_n followed by inclusion n+1. Let C_tel consist only of q(P) and q(P)[1] for these concrete telescopes. There exist e:F(O_Y[1]) isomorphic to O_Z[1] and isomorphisms alpha_X:F(Qh_Y(X))->Qh_Z(H(X)) for X in C_tel, natural for stage-induced morphisms between such objects only. For each flat telescope P and X=q(P), alpha_(X[1]);commShift_G(X) equals F(commShift_Qh_Y(X));b(Qh_Y(X));alpha_X[1], where G=H then Qh_Z, and b(K)=F(c_Y(K)^(-1));delta_F(O_Y[1],K);(e tensor id);c_Z(F(K)). Naturality for arbitrary homotopy morphisms is not asserted. No comparison for arbitrary K-flat representatives, no extension to other homotopy objects, and no natural automorphism of F is asserted.

proof.text: Bounded-above flat stages, their countable sum, and their transition cone are K-flat. Termwise tensor pullback preserves the sum and cone and its K-flat counit computes derived pullback on these representatives. The unit and shifted unit have the usual degree-zero and translated models.

Choose the unit normalization by the supplied monoidal unit map. Rewrite translation by the shifted unit using the first-variable Koszul comparison and translated left unitor. Construct e and the comparisons jointly. Expand tensorator associativity and both unit equations on the two cone summands: their transition, inclusion and projection maps commute, yielding the displayed shift equation.

For a compatible family of bounded-flat stage maps, the same equations on each stage commute with its sum map and the induced cone map. Translation preserves these equations. Common K-flat presentation comparisons give independence under homotopy isomorphisms, hence precisely naturality for the stage-induced maps. No extension to arbitrary homotopy maps is taken here.
